findings.where: Screen 12 (Mixed: a mains coil): task, card title 'A coil on 230 V, 50 Hz' and Why
findings.what: The puzzle says 'a coil' and makes '3.33 A and 0 W' the right answer, but 0 W (and X_L = 230 ÷ 4 = 57.5 Ω exactly) holds only for an ideal coil. A real mains coil drawing 4 A has wire resistance and takes some watts, and the lesson's own practice text says 'An ideal coil averages 0 W'. Say 'an ideal coil' in the task, the card title and the Why.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Down to steady DC), the wave and power graphs
findings.what: While the amber dot runs down the X_L line to 0 Hz, the voltage, current and power graphs stay as 50 Hz sine waves. So the picture never shows the cause the text gives: a flat current, a flat tangent and no back-emf. Flatten or fade the waves as the dot reaches DC.

findings.where: Screens 1 and 3, the readout rows under the graphs
findings.what: The tangent's steepness is never given a number, so Dan only sees 'voltage = L × steepness' as two shapes that match. One row at 0 ms such as '3,142 A/s × 0.0318 H = 100 V' would let him check the rule by hand.

The screen before each puzzle states its answer. Screen 1's text says 'By 5 ms ... the voltage is 0', and screen 3's bracket and row say the voltage leads by a quarter cycle. Neither puzzle asks him to predict anything. Hold back screen 1's 5 ms result, or ask about an instant the demonstration did not state.

findings.where: Explain, second paragraph, and Practice, the 'Textbooks add' line
findings.what: The lesson's central rule (the coil's voltage is L × the rate of change of its current) and 'motor windings, contactor coils and transformer windings are coils' are given only as 'textbooks add'. The research already holds Kuphaldt's quote, 'inductors oppose changes in current through them, by dropping a voltage directly proportional to the rate of change of current' (notes 3.4), and Matrix on motors (notes 3.9). Footnote them, and name Calculus fundamentals lesson 5's v = L di/dt as the maths being reused, as the brief planned.
'60 Hz is the frequency most common on board ship' is stated flat. The brief says every sea fact is labelled with its source on screen, here a marine college's notes (secondary).

findings.where: The interactive as a whole, against the brief (section 3, lesson 4, and the lessons table)
findings.what: Three things the brief promised are missing. There is no inductance slider, so L's part in X_L = 2πfL is never moved. Kuphaldt's cited 10 mH table (3.77 Ω at 60 Hz, 7.54 Ω at 120 Hz) is not used, and neither is C&G's 20 mH at 50 Hz = 6.28 Ω. So every coil on screen is an example value, and no on-screen figure can be checked against a source.

findings.where: Practice, first bullet (the 318 V safety example)
findings.what: 'Isolate before you test or touch a coil's circuit' does not match the hazard it is paired with. The 318 V appears at the moment a coil's current is broken, across the opening contacts, and isolating is itself an act that breaks the current. Say plainly that the kick comes when the circuit is broken, so the advice and the hazard line up. The arithmetic, 0.0318 × 10 ÷ 0.001 = 318 V, is right.

findings.where: Coil drawing, flux label (screens 1, 3 and 7 while dragging)
findings.what: 'no flux this instant' shows whenever the current is below about 1.1 A, which is where the flux lines' width cut-off sits. At 0.3 ms the label reads 'no flux this instant' while the row beside it reads 0.94 A. Show the label only at the zero crossing, or keep thin flux lines down to zero.

findings.where: Lead line above the stepper; screen 12's mains card
findings.what: The lead line says 'An ideal coil of 31.8 mH ... on a 100 V peak supply' on every screen, including screen 12, where the picture is a 230 V mains coil. The mains card's waves also have no scale and never say they are drawn at their peak (about 325 V), which the brief asks to be said on every screen.
Each paragraph runs about 85 to 100 words, so on a 360 px phone the picture starts well below the fold. Trim each one to its one cause and its one instruction, and let the picture carry the rest.

findings.where: Right answers on screens 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12, the '?' rows under the graphs
findings.what: On a right Check, the '?' rows vanish at once and their space stays blank until the answer rows fade in 1.2 to 1.4 s later. Cross-fade them so nothing blinks out.
